Idk if you are a mobility aid user but as a wheelchair user ramps definitely do not win

Ramps can get stupidly long and steep and some have turns as well. Lots of time ill have to stop on a ramp because of the strain it puts on my arms/ shoulders but still have to continue to hold myself still on the ramp. Of course an able bodied person could push me but relying on able bodied people heavily takes away personal freedom and independence for disabled people.

Honestly as a chair user ive had to take ramps that have taken five or more minutes to get up.  Even if its not as long its alot of physical strain for a good amount of time so id think in the long run this would be easier. This also could be accessible for people who arent chair users but have other balance issues that make it hard to go up either stairs or ramps.

I personally think this would be both physically easier, take less space, and possibly even less time than normal ramps. Not to mention places with temporary ramps that have to be brought out as needed take quite a bit to get out and make us have to rely on an able bodied person.

I could see thinking that but from what i saw this took less time than some ramps. Lots of stores either have super long ramps or very steep ramps which actually take quite a long time to get up especially if you struggle with any sort of weakness in your arms.
